meeting_header:
Date: 2025-06-11
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Orchid Labs - Lead ML Eng), Theo Park (Orchid Labs - Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Orchid Labs - CTO)
summary: Intro + quickstart SDK walkthrough (Python & TypeScript), auth patterns (API keys, SSO/SAML), environment setup (env vars, CONSOLE preview), and light demo of Console + Optimize suggestions. Agreed to pilot with Dedicated capacity evaluation and a perf benchmark. Action items and pricing to be shared.
topics: API key vs SSO for prod onboarding
Console walkthrough: routes, tokens, Optimize hints
Pilot scope: Dedicated vs Hosted, perf benchmarks
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we got about an hour so we'll walk through the SDK quickstarts then hop into the Console and Optimize tips.
[00:18] Marta: Thanks Jordan, excited. Short intro, we're trying to get predictions into our ingestion pipeline, low latency but cost sensitive.
[00:35] Jordan: Got it, cost vs latency is the theme. Priya will show a Python quickstart and a small TypeScript example too.
[01:05] Priya: Quick note, our packages are published as 'redwood-inference' on pip and '@redwood/inference' on npm in the quickstart. pip install redwood-inference, npm i @redwood/inference — should be straightforward.
[02:15] Theo: Quick question on keys — we don't want long-lived keys in code. What's the best practice?
[02:35] Priya: Short answer: env vars + secrets manager. We recommend REDWOOD_API_KEY in the environment and Rotate with your KMS. For private deploys you can also use customer-managed KMS; we support HSM backed keys.
[03:10] Marta: And SSO/SAML for teams? We have strict provisioning.
[03:28] Jordan: Yes, SSO via SAML or OIDC is supported for the Console and RBAC for token issuance. Priya do you wanna show the sample repo where we wire SSO?
[03:45] Priya: Sure — demoing the repo now, note the example uses NODE_ENV=production and REDWOOD_API_KEY env var. For server side we suggest server-to-server tokens rotated by CI. The sample GitHub action shows token rotation.
[05:10] Theo: If we go Dedicated, is the token flow different? We need to ensure tokens never leave our VPC.
[05:30] Jordan: With Redwood Private/Dedicated you can keep the control plane in your VPC or run the on-prem package. You can integrate with your internal STS to mint short-lived tokens. We also provide audit logs and token scopes in the Console.
[06:20] Marta: Okay, show us the Python quickstart.
[06:28] Priya: Opening the Python example: from redwood_inference import Client; client = Client(api_key=os.environ.get("REDWOOD_API_KEY")); resp = client.generate(model="open-llama-7b", prompt="Summarize this...") — that's the pattern. Note the import path in the repo sometimes transcribed as redwood-inferance in older versions, watch the pip version.
[08:15] Liam: What's the recommended way to embed in a K8s cron job?
[08:30] Priya: Use a service account with a short token fetched via an init container; don't bake API keys into images. Also set up per-route rate limits in the Console so your worker can't blow budget.
[09:40] Jordan: Now TypeScript — basic usage: import { RedwoodClient } from '@redwood/inference'; const client = new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.chat.create({ model: 'redwood-chat-medium', messages: [...] });
[11:00] Marta: Any gotchas with streaming in TS?
[11:10] Priya: Streams require using the event stream helper in the SDK; node-fetch vs native fetch differences can surface — we included both examples. Also watch for chunked responses in proxy setups, nginx sometimes buffers.
[12:30] Theo: Let's pivot to Console. Can we see route configs, token usage breakdown?
[12:45] Jordan: Yep — opening Console. The Routes view shows per-route latency and token cost, you can pin a model variant per route. Optimize will surface batching and caching suggestions.
[14:05] Priya: Quick demo: Optimize flagged that your 'summarize' route had 81% prefix repetition — recommend enabling prefix KV cache and a small batch window. There was a sample tile that shows estimated cost savings.
[16:00] Marta: When Optimize gives recommendations, can we auto-apply?
[16:14] Jordan: You can preview and apply. For production we'd suggest canary first. You can also tie recommendations to evaluations, the eval runner will re-run on canaries.
[18:30] Theo: We're concerned about model variant mismatch during fallback — e.g., if we pick redwood-chat-medium and fallback to a quantized variant how do you preserve output format?
[18:50] Priya: We expose model families and sanitized invariants; we also provide structured outputs and function-calling compatibility flags. If you use function-like calls or JSON schemas, we recommend specifying the schema and testing fallback variants in the eval harness.
[20:00] Liam: Could you run a quick end-to-end from code to Console route?
[20:12] Priya: Yep, running the TypeScript example and hitting the route — shows up in Console logs within a few seconds. You can filter by token usage and inspect the trace to see batching and rebatched requests.
[22:40] Marta: We have a heavy embedding workload — how do we measure unit cost?
[22:58] Jordan: Console shows embedding units and cost per 1k vectors. Also Optimize suggests vector cache and reuse patterns. For large embeddings we recommend vector pruning and approximate nearest neighbors outside hot path.
[24:30] Theo: For our compliance team, we need audit logs and retention controls.
[24:45] Jordan: Audit logs are available for Dedicated and Private. Retention policies can be configured and we support S3 archival. Also we can turn on field-level redaction for PII in logs.
[26:10] Marta: Does Redwood redact by default on hosted?
[26:20] Jordan: Hosted has configurable ingestion redaction; Dedicated gives you more control. We can share the security pack doc.
[28:45] Priya: Back to SDK: the quickstart repo includes a sample dockerfile and k8s manifest. One common typo: 'KV cash' in older slides — it's 'KV cache', sorry for the misread. Also a note on quantization flags — the client optionally passes quantize: true to the model create call when your runtime supports it.
[30:00] Liam: About benchmarks — we want to run a 1k token test at p95 latency. Can Redwood help with a perf harness?
[30:18] Jordan: Yes, our SE team can share a harness. Priya will share a lightweight harness that runs in your env and streams logs back. We usually do a baseline on hosted then Dedicated to compare.
[32:50] Marta: Any vendor lock-in concerns? We have multi-cloud requirements.
[33:05] Jordan: The API surface is standard REST/SDK, we support multi-region routing. For Private deployments you keep data and control plane on prem. You can export models and configs; we emphasize portability.
[35:00] Theo: Can Optimize explain how it got the suggestion? We need auditability.
[35:12] Priya: Optimize provides a reasoning pane — shows sample calls, token distributions, and the estimated savings math. It's not opaque.
[36:40] Marta: Show me how a canary rollout looks in Console.
[36:52] Jordan: Creating a route and adding a canary: pick the percentage, tie the fallback policy — you can also set automatic rollback on error rate or latency regression.
[38:10] Liam: Question on function calling and structured output. We rely on strict JSON schemas.
[38:25] Priya: We recommend using the function/tooling API and schema validation on the client; Redwood's runtime preserves the tokens for the schema and will surface schema validation errors in the trace.
[40:05] Theo: Any special headers for tracing?
[40:15] Jordan: X-Request-ID plus the Redwood-Trace header. We also integrate with OpenTelemetry — the Console can ingest traces.
[42:10] Marta: Security review — SSO provisioning and least privilege — can you show the org roles?
[42:25] Priya: Org admin, developer, viewer, billing. You can scope API keys to routes and sets of models. For SAML there's attribute mapping for groups.
[44:00] Theo: We're using internal KMS, can Redwood call our KMS for encryption-at-rest for the dedicated data plane?
[44:18] Jordan: Yes, for Private deployments you can configure CMEK and HSM integrations. We can include the integration checklist in the security docs.
[46:00] Marta: A couple of minor gotchas we ran into: node-fetch buffering and timeouts, and the default batch window was too aggressive for our low-latency path.
[46:20] Priya: Good notes — you can set per-route batch windows and min-latency settings. We can share our recommended configs for low-latency interactive paths.
[48:30] Liam: What's the SLA on Dedicated?
[48:40] Jordan: We have a 99.9% uptime SLA for Dedicated with latency targets depending on the capacity tier. I'll send the SLA doc.
[50:30] Theo: If we need to POC private deploy on-prem, what's the rough timeline?
[50:45] Jordan: Typical pilot 4–6 weeks: discovery, infra prep, pilot deploy, benchmark. For faster tests we can do hosted + dedicated comparison in 1–2 weeks.
[52:15] Marta: Let's talk pricing briefly.
[52:30] Jordan: Hosted is usage-based per-token/embedding. Dedicated has a reserved capacity commit and lower unit costs. We'll send a worksheet showing break-even points at volumes you gave us.
[54:00] Priya: Wrapping up SDK side: repo links, sample env file, docker + k8s manifests, quickstart readme.
[55:20] Marta: Great, we'll run the harness and return results. Also need the security pack.
[56:00] Jordan: Action items recap: Priya sends repos, Jordan sends pricing and SLA, Marta runs perf test. Any final questions?
[56:40] Liam: One last thing — what about cost alerts?
[56:50] Jordan: Console has budget alerts and per-route thresholds; we also integrate with SNS/webhooks for spikes.
[58:10] Theo: Thanks everyone — that was helpful. We'll aim to have the pilot sign-off next week.
[61:50] Jordan: Thanks all, meeting end.

Notes: transcription includes minor mis-hears (node-fetch vs native fetch, redwood-inferance typo), occasional speaker overlap. References: quickstart repo (link shared in chat), Dedicated pricing worksheet (shared after call), security pack (link to doc).
